title: Dhammadinna
hookLine: foremost among nuns in teaching; the Buddha says he would have answered as she did (MN 44)

lines: HIS FORMER WIFE, NOW A NUN.
cards: A man goes to see a nun, and he brings questions. He's Visakha, a lay follower, and he isn't a stranger to her: the commentaries say she had been his wife before she went forth. Her name is Dhammadinna.
He sits to one side and starts asking. What is identity? Where does it come from?
What path ends it? She answers each one, cleanly. And he keeps going, question after question, until he goes one question too far.
This Visakha, by the way, is a man. The laywoman Visakha comes in a few days.

teach.b: First, the questions, in the forty-fourth discourse of the Middle Length collection. They aren't easy.
Visakha asks what identity is, and she answers that the teaching calls it the five aggregates people cling to: body, feeling, perception, formations and consciousness.
He asks about the noble eightfold path, about meditation, about pleasant and painful feeling and what tendency lies under each one. Her answers are short and exact. Second, the edge.
At last he asks: what is the counterpart of nibbana? She stops him.

Friend Visakha, you've gone too far; you couldn't find the limit of your questions. The holy life is grounded in nibbana and ends in nibbana. If you wish, go and ask the Buddha, and remember what he tells you.
Third, the endorsement. Visakha goes and tells the Buddha the whole conversation. The Buddha says: Dhammadinna is wise, of great wisdom.
If you had asked me, I would have answered exactly as she did. That is the meaning; remember it so. Fourth, her title.
In the list of foremost disciples, Dhammadinna is named first among the nuns who teach the Dhamma. And notice the echo. Three days ago, Khema answered a king, and the Buddha's answer matched hers.
Today the Buddha says it again: the same.
The texts make the point twice, on purpose or not: a woman taught, and the teaching stood. She taught him.

how: The Culavedalla Sutta, Dhammadinna's dialogue with Visakha, is studied in Theravada monasteries and Buddhist study groups as a short, careful teaching on identity, the path and feeling.

o: a nun foremost in teaching the Dhamma
a monk who memorized the discourses
a gift of teaching given at a funeral

p: the question that went too far

s: the Buddha corrected one of Dhammadinna's answers
he said he would have answered exactly as she did.
in this discourse, a nun does the teaching
Visakha asks, Dhammadinna answers, and the Buddha confirms at the end.
the Visakha here is the laywoman Visakha
this Visakha is a man; the commentaries say he had been Dhammadinna's husband.

games.q: you're Dhammadinna. Visakha's questions keep coming, and now he asks for the counterpart of nibbana. what do you do?
o: tell him he's gone too far, and he may ask the Buddha.
end the conversation without a word.
games.why: she tells him he has gone too far, that the holy life ends in nibbana, and sends him to the Buddha, who says he would have answered the same.

practice: Think of someone who taught you something that held up, and who also knew where to stop: who said, that's enough for today, or, go and ask someone who knows more.
Put what they taught you into one plain sentence, silently, and let thanks come if it comes.

wordCard.voice: Dhammadinna. The nun named foremost in teaching, whose answers the Buddha said he would have given himself. Today's word.

orig.note: Pali Dhammadinna, the nun's name as it appears in the suttas.

carryVoice: Your line: she taught him. Her answers needed no correcting. Day seven hundred fifty-nine, done.

sources.ref: Anguttara Nikaya 1.14 (Dhammadinna foremost among nuns who teach the Dhamma)
